pharm: Semisynthetic aminoglycoside; binds the 30S ribosomal subunit to inhibit bacterial protein synthesis (bactericidal)
quick: 4-6.5 mg/kg/day IV/IM, in 1-3 divided doses, by indication and severity
Small amounts in milk; poorly absorbed orally by infant; use with caution
Reduce dose/extend interval; nephrotoxic, adjust to renal function and levels
No specific adjustment; minimal hepatic handling
Serum levels (peak/trough), renal function, audiometry, vestibular function
summary: Netilmicin is a semisynthetic aminoglycoside antibiotic active against many aerobic Gram-negative bacilli, including some gentamicin-resistant strains, and used parenterally for serious infections. Like other aminoglycosides it is bactericidal and carries dose-related risks of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, requiring therapeutic drug monitoring. It is not FDA-approved; dosing reflects EMA/SmPC and BNF sources.
indications: Treatment of serious infections caused by susceptible Gram-negative bacteria (e.g., septicemia, complicated urinary tract infections, lower respiratory tract, intra-abdominal, skin and soft tissue, and bone infections)
Often used in combination with a beta-lactam for serious or polymicrobial infection and for suspected Gram-negative sepsis

dosage.c: Serious systemic infection (adult, normal renal function)
dosage.d: 4 to 6 mg/kg/day; commonly given as a single daily dose or divided every 8-12 hours
dosage.t: IV infusion over 30-120 minutes or by IM injection
dosage.n: Once-daily (extended-interval) dosing is widely used; individualize by levels

dosage.d: Up to 7.5 mg/kg/day in divided doses, reduced as soon as clinically indicated
Lower end of the range, e.g., 4 mg/kg/day
Reduce the dose and/or extend the dosing interval according to creatinine clearance and serum levels

admin: Administer by slow intravenous infusion (over 30 minutes to 2 hours) or by deep intramuscular injection
Do not mix in the same syringe or infusion with beta-lactam antibiotics (inactivation)
Ensure adequate hydration to reduce nephrotoxicity
Measure serum peak and trough concentrations to guide dosing, especially with renal impairment, the elderly, or prolonged therapy
Assess baseline and periodic renal function, hearing, and vestibular function
moa: Netilmicin is a bactericidal aminoglycoside that diffuses across the bacterial outer membrane and is actively transported into the cell, where it binds irreversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit. This causes misreading of messenger RNA and inhibits bacterial protein synthesis, leading to cell death. Its activity is concentration-dependent with a post-antibiotic effect, supporting extended-interval dosing.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to netilmicin or other aminoglycosides

preg: Aminoglycosides cross the placenta and can cause irreversible bilateral congenital deafness in the fetus. Netilmicin should be avoided in pregnancy unless the benefit clearly outweighs the risk in a serious or life-threatening infection.
lact: Netilmicin is excreted in breast milk in small amounts and is poorly absorbed from the infant gastrointestinal tract. Use with caution; monitor the breastfed infant for gastrointestinal disturbance.
renal: Netilmicin is eliminated almost entirely by the kidneys and is nephrotoxic. Reduce the dose and/or lengthen the dosing interval in renal impairment based on creatinine clearance, and adjust using serum peak and trough concentrations. Maintain hydration and avoid other nephrotoxins.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is required for hepatic impairment because netilmicin is not significantly metabolized by the liver.

major: Other nephrotoxic or ototoxic drugs (loop diuretics such as furosemide, amphotericin B, vancomycin, cisplatin, ciclosporin) - additive toxicity
Neuromuscular blocking agents (potentiation of neuromuscular blockade and respiratory depression)
moderate: Beta-lactams (physical inactivation if mixed; give separately)
minor: May potentiate the effect of anticoagulants in some patients
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum creatinine, BUN, and urinary casts; can cause electrolyte disturbances (low potassium, calcium, magnesium)

serious: Ototoxicity - cochlear (hearing loss, tinnitus) and vestibular (vertigo, ataxia), which may be irreversible
emergency: Acute hearing loss, severe vertigo, or balance disturbance - stop and seek urgent evaluation
Neuromuscular weakness or respiratory difficulty - emergency care

monitoring: Serum peak and trough concentrations to keep within the therapeutic range and avoid toxicity
Serum creatinine and creatinine clearance before and during therapy
Audiometry and vestibular assessment, especially with prolonged therapy or risk factors
Fluid balance, electrolytes (potassium, calcium, magnesium), and urine output
Signs of neuromuscular weakness, particularly in at-risk patients
counsel: This antibiotic is given by injection or drip in hospital and your blood levels and kidney function will be checked
Report any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, dizziness, or balance problems straight away
Tell staff if you notice reduced urination or swelling
Report rash, itching, or difficulty breathing
Drink adequate fluids unless told otherwise
pk: Bactericidal effect during the infusion; concentration-dependent killing
Peak serum concentration at the end of an IV infusion or about 30-60 minutes after IM
Approximately 2 to 2.5 hours (markedly prolonged in renal impairment)
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from light per product labeling
pearls: Not FDA-approved; dosing and indications are based on EMA/SmPC and BNF sources
Semisynthetic aminoglycoside that may retain activity against some gentamicin-resistant Gram-negative bacteria
Dose-related nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity (cochlear and vestibular) require therapeutic drug monitoring
Extended-interval (once-daily) dosing exploits concentration-dependent killing and the post-antibiotic effect
Avoid in myasthenia gravis and do not mix in the same line as beta-lactams
missed: Doses are administered by a healthcare professional on a fixed schedule with level monitoring. If a dose is delayed, the clinical team will adjust timing; do not attempt to self-administer or make up doses.
overdose: Overdose increases the risk of nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, and neuromuscular blockade. Management is supportive; hemodialysis (and to a lesser extent peritoneal dialysis) can remove netilmicin from the blood, and calcium salts or anticholinesterases may reverse neuromuscular blockade. Contact Poison Control or local toxicology services.
